title: Void Ending in a Sextile to Sun
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The sextile is one of the two friendly aspects. Picatrix ties the Moon to the fortunes by trine and sextile whenever a work is meant to prosper, and grades the sextile as the aspect of moderate friendship: the signs it joins are kin in action but not in passion, so the concord between them is a lukewarm one.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a sextile to Sun, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his light and his generative heat. Picatrix calls the Sun the light of the world and the axis on which the universe turns; generative power flows from him, the heart is his seat in the body, gold is his metal, and the ruby and the jacinth his stones. His benevolence fits great royal achievements and kings. The whole lunar doctrine hangs on him, for in the text's accounting the stars and the Moon together sustain all vegetation and every composite body.
